method.method_draft: Use an explicit algebraic reconstruction of the parabola. From the text, the line is y1 = -x + 3, so its x-intercept is B = (3, 0) and its y-intercept is C = (0, 3). The parabola passes through B and has axis of symmetry x = 2, so its other x-intercept A is symmetric to B about x = 2, giving A = (1, 0). Write y2 = k(x - 1)(x - 3). Since C = (0, 3) lies on the parabola, 3 = k(-1)(-3), hence k = 1. Thus y2 = (x - 1)(x - 3). Solve y1 < y2: -x + 3 < x^2 - 4x + 3, so x^2 - 3x > 0, i.e. x(x - 3) > 0. Therefore x < 0 or x > 3.
